\begin{document}
\Lesson{29}{Point Kinetics with Feedback}{FNRP 5.6 and 9.5}
{After a positive reactivity insertion, what determines whether neutron density settles at a higher level or rises to a peak and falls?}

\begin{handoutflow}
\Sec{1}{Start from critical equilibrium}

For one precursor group and no external neutron source, the neutron density $n$ and effective precursor concentration $C$ obey
$$
  \dot n=\frac{\rho-\beta}{\Lambda}\,n+\lambda C,
  \qquad \dot C=\frac{\beta}{\Lambda}\,n-\lambda C .
$$
At $t=0^-$, $\rho=0$, $n=n_0$, and $C=C_0=\beta n_0/(\lambda\Lambda)$.
A step insertion changes $\dot n$ at once. Both $n$ and $C$ are continuous.

\textbf{Recall from Lesson 28.} For constant $\rho$, try $n,C\propto e^{\omega t}$. Rearranging the characteristic equation gives the one-group inhour relation
$$
\omega^2+\left(\lambda-\frac{\rho-\beta}{\Lambda}\right)\omega
  -\frac{\lambda\rho}{\Lambda}=0
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\rho=\omega\!\left(\Lambda+\frac{\beta}{\omega+\lambda}\right).
$$
When fuel heats up, $\rho$ changes during the insertion. The instantaneous growth rate $\dot n/n$ then depends on both $\rho(t)$ and the precursor inventory.

\Sec{2}{Let the fuel temperature set reactivity}

Write $\theta=T_f-T_{f0}$ for the fuel temperature rise and $\rho_{\rm ext}$ for the imposed reactivity. With $\theta(0)=0$,
$$
  \boxed{\rho(t)=\rho_{\rm ext}(t)+\alpha_f\,\theta(t)},
  \qquad \alpha_f=-3\times10^{-5}\ {\rm K}^{-1}.
$$
A 100 K rise thus offsets a 300 pcm insertion. Here $1\ {\rm pcm}=10^{-5}$ in reactivity, and one dollar is $\beta$.

Write $p=n/n_0=P/P_0$ for relative power at fixed flux shape and spectrum. A lumped heat balance with fixed coolant temperature $T_c$ reads
$$
 C_{\rm th}\dot T_f=P_0 p-H(T_f-T_c).
$$
$C_{\rm th}$ is the fuel heat capacity (J/K) and $H$ the fuel-to-coolant thermal conductance (W/K).

\textbf{Model A. Fast heat removal.}
In the quasistatic limit, heat removed balances power at each instant. Subtract the initial balance $H(T_{f0}-T_c)=P_0$ to get
$$
 \theta=A(p-1),\qquad \dot\theta=A\dot p,\qquad A=P_0/H.
$$

\textbf{Model B. Adiabatic fuel.}
Neglect heat removal during the transient. Deposited energy accumulates as sensible heat.
$$
 \dot\theta=Bp,\qquad \theta(t)=B\!\int_0^t p(s)\,ds,
 \qquad B=P_0/C_{\rm th}.
$$
Both cases start from the same critical neutron state. For B, assume cooling balanced $P_0$ before $t=0$ and ceases at the start of the run. Thus $\dot\theta(0^+)=B$ even at $p=1$.

\columnbreak
\Sec{3}{Add one state to Lesson 28's solver}

Use $\mathbf y=(n,C,\theta)$. The notebook supplies $\beta$, $\Lambda$, $\lambda$, $n_0$, and $\alpha_f$. Set $A=100$ K for the reference fuel-to-coolant temperature difference. Use $B=240$ K/s, corresponding to $P_0/V\simeq720$ W/cm$^3$ and $C_{\rm th}/V\simeq3$ J/(cm$^3$ K). The \texttt{fixed} case holds $T_f=T_{f0}$.

\begin{lstlisting}[style=feedback python]
import numpy as np
from scipy.integrate import solve_ivp

beta, Lambda = 0.0065, 1e-4            # Lambda in s
lam = np.log(2) / 5.0                  # 1/s
alpha = -3e-5                          # 1/K
A, B = 100.0, 240.0                    # K, K/s
n0 = 1e9                               # 1/cm^3
y0 = [n0, beta*n0/(lam*Lambda), 0.0]  # n, C, theta

def f(t, y, rho_ext, model):
    n, C, theta = y
    rho = rho_ext + alpha*theta
    dn = (rho - beta)*n/Lambda + lam*C
    dC = beta*n/Lambda - lam*C
    if model == "A":
        dT = A*dn/n0
    elif model == "B":
        dT = B*n/n0
    elif model == "fixed":
        dT = 0.0
    else:
        raise ValueError("Use A, B, or fixed")
    return dn, dC, dT

def solve(rho_ext, times, model, start=y0):
    sol = solve_ivp(f, (times[0], times[-1]), start,
                    args=(rho_ext, model), t_eval=times,
                    method="LSODA", rtol=1e-8, atol=1e-9)
    if not sol.success:
        raise RuntimeError(sol.message)
    return sol.y
\end{lstlisting}

\textbf{Apply the 300 pcm insertion for 5 s.}
Restart at the withdrawal time with the final state of the first solve. The stored fuel heat and precursor inventory carry over.
\begin{lstlisting}[style=feedback python]
t1 = np.linspace(0, 5, 1001)
t2 = np.linspace(5, 10, 1001)
one = solve(0.003, t1, "B")
two = solve(0.0, t2, "B", one[:, -1])
\end{lstlisting}

\textbf{Start a fresh prompt excursion.} Hold $\rho_{\rm ext}=1.5\beta$ for the full interval shown. Replace \texttt{"B"} with \texttt{"A"} or \texttt{"fixed"} to compare the three curves on page 2.
\begin{lstlisting}[style=feedback python]
tp = np.linspace(0, 0.20, 501)        # seconds
n, C, theta = solve(1.5*beta, tp, "B")
p = n/n0
dollars = (1.5*beta + alpha*theta)/beta
\end{lstlisting}
\end{handoutflow}

\Sec{4}{Insert 300 pcm, then withdraw it at 5 s}
The same positive insertion brings all three cases to $\rho/\beta=0.462$ at $t=0^+$. Read each density history alongside its net reactivity. The vertical guide marks withdrawal.
\par\noindent\plotstart
\begin{axis}[feedback axis,xmin=0,xmax=10,xtick={0,2,4,6,8,10},xlabel={Time (s)},
 ymin=0,ymax=3.6,ytick={0,1,2,3},ylabel={Relative neutron density $n/n_0$}]
\draw[black!45,densely dotted] (axis cs:5,0)--(axis cs:5,3.6);
\traces{\milddata}{n}
\end{axis}\plotend\hfill\plotstart
\begin{axis}[feedback axis,xmin=0,xmax=10,xtick={0,2,4,6,8,10},xlabel={Time (s)},
 ymin=-3.6,ymax=.8,ytick={-3,-2,-1,0},ylabel={Net reactivity $\rho/\beta$}]
\draw[black!45,densely dotted] (axis cs:5,-3.6)--(axis cs:5,.8);
\traces{\milddata}{r}
\end{axis}\plotend

\textbf{At withdrawal.} Just before 5 s, $n/n_0$ is 3.33 at fixed $T_f$, 1.56 in A, and 0.225 in B.
Removing the insertion lowers $\rho$ by the same 300 pcm in every case. In Model A the fuel cools as power falls. In Model B it keeps heating as long as fissions deposit energy.

\Sec{5}{Hold a prompt-supercritical insertion of 1.50 dollars}
Here $\rho_{\rm ext}=975$ pcm exceeds $\beta=650$ pcm. At fixed temperature the prompt term has an e-folding time of $\Lambda/(\rho_{\rm ext}-\beta)=31$ ms. Follow the adiabatic curve from the prompt-critical crossing (right) to the density peak (left).
\par\noindent\plotstart
\begin{axis}[feedback axis,xmin=0,xmax=200,xtick={0,50,100,150,200},xlabel={Time (ms)},
 restrict y to domain*=-1:18,ymin=0,ymax=15.5,ytick={0,3,6,9,12,15},ylabel={Relative neutron density $n/n_0$}]
\traces{\promptdata}{n}
\fill[modelB] (axis cs:73.24,12.993) circle[radius=2pt];
\node[anchor=south west,font=\fontsize{8}{9}\selectfont,text=modelB] at (axis cs:75,13.0) {peak at 73.2 ms};
\end{axis}\plotend\hfill\plotstart
\begin{axis}[feedback axis,xmin=0,xmax=200,xtick={0,50,100,150,200},xlabel={Time (ms)},
 ymin=0,ymax=1.67,ytick={0,.5,1,1.5},ylabel={Net reactivity $\rho/\beta$}]
\draw[black!50,densely dotted] (axis cs:0,1)--(axis cs:200,1);
\traces{\promptdata}{r}
\fill[modelB] (axis cs:67.53,1) circle[radius=2pt];
\node[anchor=south west,font=\fontsize{8}{9}\selectfont,text=modelB] at (axis cs:70,1) {67.5 ms};
\end{axis}\plotend

\textbf{Why does the peak come later?} At $\rho=\beta$ the prompt term vanishes, but $\dot n=\lambda C>0$.
Model B reaches this threshold after a fuel temperature rise of $(975-650)/3\simeq108$ K. Density peaks at $13.0\,n_0$ when $\rho/\beta\simeq0.918$ and the prompt loss just balances $\lambda C$. With $T_f$ fixed, density has already reached $76.3\,n_0$ by 100 ms, above the plotted range.

\begin{checkpoint}[Two checks on the curves]
\textbf{After withdrawal at fixed temperature,} add the neutron and precursor equations to show that
$\frac{d}{dt}(n+C)=\rho n/\Lambda$. Which inventory is conserved after 5 s? Use the inventory at withdrawal and $C_\infty=\beta n_\infty/(\lambda\Lambda)$ to explain why $n$ settles near $1.80\,n_0$.

\smallskip
\textbf{If the 1.50-dollar insertion stays in,} a positive steady power requires $\rho=0$. Use Model A to predict the eventual $n/n_0$. Which term in Model B prevents a steady fuel temperature at positive power?
\end{checkpoint}
